campaign.mission: Identify magnetically recoverable microplastic-remediation designs that can outperform or de-risk the Ti3C2Tx@Ni reference without promoting unvalidated safety claims.

candidates.label: Ti3C2Tx@Ni reference
risk_flags: nickel ion release / secondary pollution requires resolution
complete magnetic retrieval is not guaranteed
field soil, natural water, mixed-pollutant and repeated-cycle validation remain open
candidates.score_semantics: heuristic research-priority score; not efficacy or safety

candidates.label: Ti3C2Tx + Fe3O4
risk_flags: no direct MXene-Fe3O4 microplastic-removal validation in this evidence seed
iron-oxide nanoparticle fate and ecotoxicity remain matrix- and dose-dependent
particle loss must be quantified by mass balance
candidates.score_semantics: heuristic research-priority score; not efficacy or safety

kill_criteria: microplastic removal fails to reproduce above passive-adsorbent control
material recovery is incomplete beyond a pre-registered tolerance
measurable secondary contamination exceeds the pre-registered safety threshold
performance collapses during repeated cycles
ecotoxicity signal is materially worse than matched controls
sequence: water capture benchmark against Ti3C2Tx@Ni using polystyrene and PET controls
water-permeated soil extraction benchmark using the same polymer classes
magnetic retrieval mass balance: quantify unrecovered robot material after each run
metal/particle release assay before and after actuation
ten-cycle capture/recovery/reuse durability test
ecotoxicity screen on environmentally relevant organisms and matrix controls
mixed-polymer and natural-water challenge only after the preceding gates pass
